indicator_definition: Concentration of chlorophyll-a in coastal and transitional waters as a proxy for eutrophication. Higher concentrations indicate algal growth from nutrient pollution. Data compiled from marine monitoring programmes.
rationale: Eutrophication degrades marine ecosystems. Reducing nutrient inputs is essential for healthy seas. Progress means stable or declining chlorophyll-a concentrations.
methodology_characteristics: Data compiled from national marine monitoring and satellite remote sensing. Reported under the Marine Strategy Framework Directive and compiled by the EEA.
indicator_name: Chlorophyll-a concentration in coastal and transitional waters
graph_title: Chlorophyll-a concentration in coastal and transitional waters
